articles.title: Israeli President Isaac Herzog Selects Gadi Eisenkot to Form New Government
articles.summary: Isaac Herzog has selected Gadi Eisenkot to attempt to form a new government following last month's parliamentary elections. The move comes after the polls left neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a clear majority.
articles.content: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has selected former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to attempt to form a new government following last month's parliamentary elections. The move comes after the polls left neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a clear majority. Eisenkot is Netanyahu's strongest rival, and his selection by Herzog marks a significant development in the ongoing political stalemate. The elections saw Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition lose its majority, but it remains the largest bloc in parliament. The anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Eisenkot has refused to collaborate with Arab parties that could potentially hand them a majority. However, despite this, Arab leaders have nominated Eisenkot for the role of forming a new government after marathon talks with Herzog. Eisenkot's selection will now see him attempting to build a coalition and secure a majority in parliament, presenting a challenge to Netanyahu's bid to remain in power as Israel's longest-serving leader. The Israeli president has entrusted Gadi Eisenkot with the task of forming a government, following weeks of intense negotiations after the recent elections. As per presidential protocol, Eisenkot will now attempt to assemble a coalition in parliament, which is expected to be a complex and challenging process. With a 28-day deadline to form a government, Eisenkot has three potential pathways to power: attempting to create a minority government with support from Arab parties, forming an alliance with ultra-Orthodox groups he had previously shunned, or forging a unity government with incumbent Prime Minister Netanyahu. However, analysts suggest that all these options are unlikely to materialize. Eisenkot's selection comes as a result of the failure of Netanyahu's wider religious-nationalist coalition to secure a majority in parliament, despite winning the most seats for any single party. With only 53 seats out of a total 120, Netanyahu's chances of remaining in power appear slim. The Likud party secured 27 seats, but it was not enough to guarantee a continuation of Netanyahu's tenure. The process of forming a government is expected to be protracted, with the possibility of extensions and further negotiations. If Eisenkot fails to assemble a coalition, another candidate will be nominated to attempt to form a government, with the option of holding new elections if all else fails. Eisenkot's Yashar party secured 21 seats, emerging as the second-largest party in the election. This significant showing enabled Eisenkot to form a coalition government, comprising four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties that collectively won 48 seats. However, this tally fell short of an outright majority, leaving Eisenkot with the daunting task of assembling a stable coalition. His background as a military commander, who oversaw operations in Lebanon, has been highlighted by his campaign team as a key asset in navigating Israel's complex security landscape. Eisenkot comes from a unique cultural heritage, being the son of Moroccan immigrants, and would be the first prime minister from Israel's Mizrahi community. This demographic shift is significant, given that Jews tracing their roots to the Middle East and North Africa have historically been underrepresented in Israeli politics. The personal costs of Eisenkot's involvement in national service are also well-documented, with his family having suffered the loss of a son and two nephews during combat in Gaza since 2023. Eisenkot's views on Israel's military doctrine are at odds with his new role as prime minister-designate. He has expressed opposition to a policy known as "Dahiya Doctrine", named after a Beirut suburb devastated by war, which authorizes the use of disproportionate force against civilian infrastructure. Critics have accused Israel of committing war crimes in Gaza, where over 74,000 Palestinians have lost their lives since the assault began. However, Israel disputes these claims and maintains that its actions are justified under military necessity. articles.summary: Users can access Grok's features directly within Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides through the Extensions menu.
articles.content: SpaceXAI has made its chatbot, Grok, available as a free add-on in Google Workspace, allowing users to access its features directly within Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. The installation process is straightforward - simply head to the Google Workspace Marketplace, click on the "Add-ons tab, search for Grok, and select it from the results. Once installed, open any of the three supported apps and navigate to the Extensions menu to access Grok's functionality. From there, you can activate the add-on and start using its features. Grok's capabilities are diverse and powerful, offering a range of tools that can enhance productivity within Google Workspace. For instance, it can be used to fact-check claims and generate images, in addition to providing real-time feedback on spreadsheets by highlighting relevant cells. It also has the ability to convert outlines into slide decks and transform rough notes into formatted documents. The availability of Grok as a free add-on is likely to be of interest to Google Workspace users, but it's worth noting that there are some factors to consider before integrating it into your workflow. To install Grok in Google Workspace, navigate to the Google Workspace Marketplace where it is listed as a free add-on. Click on the Install button and select the Google account you wish to use, then proceed by clicking Continue. Alternatively, if you're already working on a file within Docs, Sheets or Slides, you can install Grok directly from the Extensions menu. Once you've initiated the installation process, you'll be prompted to grant permissions for Grok to access your Google Workspace files. Specifically, it will request see, edit, create and delete permissions for all Google Docs files and every Slides presentation in your account. However, its access is more limited when it comes to Sheets, covering only those spreadsheets where the add-on has been installed. After installation, you can access Grok's features by opening any doc, spreadsheet or presentation within Workspace and navigating to the Extensions menu. From there, select Grok" and click on "Open Grok" to bring up a side panel with its functionality. You'll then be prompted to sign in and authenticate before Grok becomes fully accessible. Once authenticated, Grok's features will be available across all three Workspace apps - Docs, Sheets, and Slides. This allows you to seamlessly integrate its capabilities into your workflow without having to switch between different tools or interfaces. Grok can seamlessly integrate into Google Docs, allowing it to write directly onto the page while performing tasks typical of language models, such as formatting text and creating lists from rough notes. However, when put to the test, Grok's output was less than polished in some cases, with a draft generated from installation instructions exhibiting noticeable AI-generated content. This is not an isolated incident, as other instances of Grok's writing have shown similar characteristics. One notable feature of Grok is its ability to track changes made within Google Docs, making it easy to review and revert back to previous versions if needed. Additionally, with Grok's connectors activated, the tool can access context from recent emails or files stored in Google Drive, though this requires granting it permission to do so. In Slides, Grok demonstrates its capabilities by building presentation decks from outlines, creating new slides that match existing themes and even researching topics from online sources. This includes pulling information from X, although some may question the reliability of such a source. To test its limits, I asked Grok to build a six-slide deck focused on its own track record for accuracy and bias since 2025, complete with cited sources on each slide and a final rating of its reliability as a source. Grok's capabilities extend beyond data analysis in Sheets. It can read selected ranges, provide answers with citations, and even insert charts into the document. Additionally, Grok can rerun scenarios when assumptions are changed, allowing users to undo changes as they would with any ordinary edit. The integration of Gemini, Google's chatbot, is also worth noting. By default, it opens from an icon at the top-right corner of various Workspace apps, including Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, and Chat. However, access to Gemini comes at a cost, as it requires eligible Workspace plans for work accounts or specific subscriptions for personal accounts. Google's decision to fold Gemini into its Business and Enterprise plans in January 2025 eliminated the need for a separate add-on that had previously increased costs by $32 per user per month. Since then, access to Gemini has become more restricted, available only through paid subscriptions. This shift also applies to Google's agent, which is now paywalled. Grok stands out from Gemini in several key areas. Firstly, it can integrate with data from X, but this feature may be seen as a double-edged sword. Additionally, Grok has limitations in terms of app access, being restricted to Docs, Sheets, and Slides compared to Gemini's wider reach across Workspace. However, users can work around these restrictions by granting Grok access to Gmail and Drive files via connectors. This allows for some flexibility in using Grok despite its limited scope. Nevertheless, the decision to use Grok ultimately depends on individual preferences regarding data integration and AI capabilities. Despite its limitations, Grok offers a simple way to add an AI side panel to Google Workspace without incurring additional costs. However, this comes with the caveat of granting it access to specific files and folders. Users must weigh these trade-offs when deciding between using Grok or Gemini. Ultimately, the choice between Grok and Gemini depends on individual needs and preferences regarding AI integration and data analysis within Google Workspace. articles.content: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has emphasized his team's need for improvement in two key areas after their narrow 1-0 win over Hull City. Arteta's comments come on the heels of a familiar scoreline that has become all too common for Arsenal this season, with many of their wins coming by just one goal. Despite securing their third 1-0 victory in four league games, Arteta acknowledged that his team could have done better, particularly in terms of finishing. The pressure is mounting on Arsenal to strengthen their squad, especially up front, as the transfer window approaches. While the club is reportedly monitoring several options and preparing to do some business, Arteta made it clear he doesn't want his players fixating on what they don't have. Arteta's solution to Arsenal's problems lies in becoming more efficient, a sentiment echoed when discussing their sixth win by one goal out of 10 Premier League games this season. The Gunners' narrow 1-0 victory over Hull City was a testament to their manager's emphasis on being more pragmatic and creating chaos in the opponent's defense. Arteta has been lamenting his team's inability to capitalize on scoring opportunities, particularly in one-on-one situations, which he believes is a crucial aspect of raising their level of performance. The manager's desire for his team to be more "chaotic and unpredictable on the pitch is a clear indication that he wants them to break free from their reliance on perfect goals and instead focus on creating a high volume of chances. This approach aligns with Arteta's reputation as a probabilities guy, who views games as equations that can be solved through precise calculations, including the team's shape and positioning. Arsenal's pressing strategy has been effective in many games this season, but it also comes at a cost. The team's high-intensity approach demands a lot of energy and can sometimes stifle creative freedom. This tension between structure and flair is a delicate balance that Arteta's team must navigate. The playmaker Martin Odegaard is an interesting case study. He has the ability to produce some truly exceptional moments on the pitch, but it seems his role has shifted somewhat under Arteta. Rather than being a key creator, he is now often praised for his understanding of the team's pressing strategy and his leadership in this area. The contrast between Odegaard's current role and his natural talents is striking. He is capable of producing moments of magic on the pitch, but they are now relatively rare. Instead, he excels at marshaling the team's defensive efforts and ensuring everyone knows where to press. Noni Madueke is another player who embodies a more chaotic approach to the game. As one of the most direct attackers in the league, he often takes players on and creates opportunities through his individual skill. This unpredictability is refreshing to watch, but it also poses challenges for Arteta's team as they try to balance their pressing strategy with creative freedom. Arsenal's attacking play has been unpredictable at times this season, making it difficult for fans and pundits to anticipate the performance level of certain players when they take to the pitch. This unpredictability is reflected in the varying levels of performance from some key attackers, with club insiders suggesting that their output can range anywhere from two to eight out of ten. One player who has been criticized for not living up to expectations is Madueke, whose runs down the wing often end with a predictable cross rather than a more creative attacking move. This lack of variation is particularly frustrating given his potential as a threat on the flank. In fact, Arteta's desire to score a perfect goal highlights one of the key issues facing Arsenal's attack, which is that they don't shoot enough and therefore fail to create enough scoring opportunities. Arsenal's impressive run in the league has seen them win nine out of ten matches, but their performance against Hull City highlights a key issue: their attacking efficiency. Despite dominating the match, they struggled to score, emphasizing the need for improvement in this area. The team's structure and organization are evident in their ability to navigate tough opponents like Hull City, who were described as respectable" by Arteta. articles.title: Study Finds Doctoral Students Need Rhetorical Agility to Write Across Different Genres
articles.summary: Researchers have found that mastering one type of text does not automatically translate to being able to write for another, posing a challenge for academics who need to communicate complex ideas.
articles.content: A new study from Chalmers University of Technology has shed light on how doctoral students can adapt their writing to reach different audiences. Researchers have found that mastering one type of text does not automatically translate to being able to write for another. This poses a challenge for academics who need to communicate complex ideas to both colleagues and non-experts. The study highlights the varying demands placed on writers depending on the context, purpose, and prior knowledge of their readers. For instance, an academic abstract requires concise and technical language, whereas a blog post may call for more engaging and accessible writing. Meanwhile, a public outreach article needs to convey complex information in a clear and simple manner. To address this challenge, researchers at Chalmers have been exploring the benefits of teaching doctoral students how to write across different genres simultaneously. By doing so, they aim to develop the "rhetorical agility needed to adapt writing styles to new contexts. According to Peter Wingrove, postdoctoral researcher and lead author of the study, this approach can help students navigate unfamiliar text types more effectively. The goal is not to teach every possible writing task that a doctoral student will encounter, but rather to equip them with the skills to approach different text types with confidence. By working with multiple genres at once, researchers believe that students can develop a deeper understanding of how to communicate complex ideas in various contexts. The workshop involved eight doctoral students who were tasked with working with three distinct text genres during a single session. The first task required them to analyze an academic abstract, identifying its intended audience, purpose, and structure. This exercise was meant to help participants understand the underlying principles of this genre. Next, the students worked in groups to transform a research blog post into an academic abstract, exploring various ways to present the content. They were given examples for reference but no explicit guidance on how to complete the task. This process allowed them to experiment with different approaches and see what worked best. The final assignment involved writing an abstract of their own research and then reworking it into a short popular science article. This exercise forced participants to adapt their writing style to reach a new audience, one that might not be familiar with technical jargon or academic terminology. They were encouraged to think creatively about how to engage this readership. The researchers analyzed the texts produced by the students, taking note of language and structural changes made in each genre. Some participants placed key findings early in their writing, while others employed storytelling techniques or used questions to capture the reader's attention. The use of technical terms was also adapted to suit the new audience. In analyzing the group discussions and interviews with the participants, the researchers found that these individuals were able to reason about their choices and identify areas where they needed to draw on existing knowledge or learn more. This ability to transfer skills between genres and adapt writing styles to different audiences is a key goal of Multi-Genre Pedagogy, an approach aimed at developing flexible writing skills and awareness of various text types. The process of making complex research accessible to a broader audience requires more than just explaining technical terms and concepts. It involves developing ideas in greater detail and acknowledging that specialists may take certain aspects for granted. According to Raffaella Negretti, professor at Chalmers University of Technology, understanding what readers need to follow the discussion is crucial. To achieve this goal, the concept of Multi-Genre Pedagogy" has been developed, aiming to equip doctoral students with flexible writing skills and awareness of various text genres. This approach enables students to adapt their writing styles to reach different audiences, a skill that can be applied across multiple disciplines. By doing so, researchers can communicate their findings more effectively, bridging the gap between academia and the general public. Ultimately, this ability to transfer skills between genres and adapt writing styles is essential for making research accessible and relevant to various stakeholders. articles.title: System Bottleneck Calculators Identify Performance Limitations
articles.summary: These tools help identify which component is limiting system performance during stress tests.
articles.content: Building and upgrading computer systems can be a daunting task, especially when it comes to ensuring that all components are compatible and working in harmony. To mitigate this complexity, bottleneck calculators have emerged as a valuable tool for system builders and upgraders alike. These tools help identify which component is limiting the rest of the system during stress tests, allowing users to pinpoint the issue and decide on the next course of action. A bottleneck occurs when one component holds back the others, hindering overall performance until the issue is resolved. For instance, if a CPU is maxing out its capacity while the GPU remains underutilized, it's likely experiencing a CPU bottleneck that's stifling the GPU's potential. Knowing which component is causing the bottleneck is crucial for deciding what to upgrade or troubleshoot next. When dealing with system bottlenecks, a common challenge is identifying which component is causing the issue. This is where online tools come in handy, offering a quick way to assess compatibility without having to stress-test your entire system. A bottleneck calculator works by comparing the performance of your chosen CPU and GPU at a specific resolution. Common benchmarks include 1080p, 1440p, and 2160p. The tool will then provide a score indicating how well each component handles the workload. If both components are capable of performing adequately at the target benchmark, you can expect a low bottleneck score, typically around ten percent or less. However, if one component is struggling to keep up, it will receive a higher percentage, signaling that it's the main culprit behind the bottleneck. In most cases, the CPU is the root cause of system bottlenecks. As the central processing unit, its primary function is to transmit information efficiently throughout the system. When it fails to do so, other components must wait for its signal, leading to stuttering in video games and other applications. A GPU bottleneck, on the other hand, typically occurs when the graphics card is overwhelmed by rendering high-resolution graphics or frame rates beyond its capabilities. This can result in screen tearing, low frame rates, and inconsistent system performance. The performance of a graphics processing unit (GPU) is heavily dependent on the number of pixels it renders per second, which explains why bottleneck calculators ask for your target resolution. However, this reliance on theoretical data from manufacturer spec sheets makes bottleneck calculators inherently unreliable. They fail to account for variability in other system components and the specific applications being tested, leading to inaccurate results. The limitations of bottleneck calculators become apparent when considering the differences between various graphics cards and their performance in different scenarios. For instance, a newer Intel GPU may struggle with older DirectX 11 applications that are easily handled by Nvidia or AMD cards. Bottleneck calculators are not designed for detailed system troubleshooting but can still be useful during system build planning. They provide a quick way to check if your chosen CPU and GPU combination can handle the desired resolution out of the box. Despite their limitations, bottleneck calculators can also serve as a fun tool for hobbyists to explore unusual hardware combinations that might not be commonly used or seen in practice. While bottleneck calculators may provide a basic understanding of how your GPU and CPU interact, they are not a foolproof method for assessing PC performance. These tools often rely on simplified calculations that can't account for various factors such as outdated drivers or background applications. A simple bottleneck percentage doesn't give the complete picture, as it fails to consider multiple variables including installed drivers and running apps that should be disabled during benchmarking. articles.title: Steam Overlay Offers Enhanced Features for Gamers
articles.summary: A significant update to Steam in 2023 introduced a revamped overlay that has set a new standard for game overlays and launchers across the industry.
articles.content: Steam users may think they're familiar with the platform's overlay feature, but a closer look reveals a wealth of capabilities beyond what meets the eye. A significant update to Steam in 2023 introduced a revamped overlay that has set a new standard for game overlays and launchers across the industry. This redesigned interface offers an impressive array of features that enhance the gaming experience. For gamers who frequently use the overlay or are looking to explore its full potential, it's surprising how much functionality is available. To access Steam's overlay while playing games, press Shift + Tab on your keyboard simultaneously. If you're new to the platform, this shortcut will open up a world of possibilities. Alternatively, you can customize the key combination from within Steam's settings menu by clicking on the 'Settings' option and navigating to the 'In-Game' section. Steam users can adjust various overlay settings, including the ability to disable it altogether if needed. The platform is also smart enough to remember individual game configurations, so gamers don't have to reorganize the interface for each new title they play. The variety of features available through Steam's overlay has set a high bar for other platforms and publishers, who are now scrambling to catch up with the industry leader. As gamers continue to explore the capabilities of Steam's redesigned overlay, it will be interesting to see how its functionality evolves in response to user feedback and emerging trends in gaming technology. The Steam overlay has become a vital part of gaming on the platform, offering a wide range of features that can enhance your overall experience. One of the most useful features is the built-in browser, which allows you to access web pages without leaving your game. This is particularly handy for checking out online guides or tutorials that might help you overcome obstacles in your current playthrough. You can easily switch between your game and the browser by pressing a shortcut at the bottom of the overlay. The Steam overlay also offers a text editor, which can be useful when playing puzzle games like Blue Prince or Tunic. This feature allows you to jot down notes as you try to piece together clues, making it easier to keep track of your progress. The editor is fairly robust, allowing you to format text and even write code blocks. The overlay's features are not just limited to in-game tools. It also includes a timer function that can help you keep track of time while gaming. This is particularly useful for those who have limited gaming sessions due to other commitments. With the built-in timer, you can set reminders to switch between games or activities. Gamers with favorite community guides will appreciate being able to access them directly from the overlay. These guides are often excellent resources that offer valuable tips and strategies for completing levels or achieving specific goals in a game. The Steam overlay offers a range of features that go beyond just providing information about the game you're playing. For instance, you can view and manage screenshots and recordings directly from within the overlay. From here, you can browse through all your captured images and videos, even those taken in other games. When you click on one, you'll have the option to save it to a folder on your computer or share it with friends over Steam chat. Sharing your gaming experiences has never been easier. With just a few clicks, you can send your screenshots and recordings directly to social media platforms or even transfer them to your smartphone via the Steam Mobile app. The overlay's sharing capabilities extend to other features as well. You can also use it to manage your saved games, view game guides, and access other in-game resources. The Steam overlay offers more than just game management features, as it also enables seamless co-operative gameplay with friends through Valve's Remote Play Together protocol. This allows up to four players to join in on local co-op games over the internet, without requiring friends to own a copy of the game themselves, provided it supports the protocol. To start a co-op session, simply navigate to the Steam overlay and click the Remote Play button. From there, you can invite your friends to join in, giving them access to control the game alongside you - even if they don't have their own controller. The best part is that they won't be able to access any other parts of your PC while Remote Play is active. articles.title: Armenia Arrests Opposition Figure Over Facebook Posts Criticizing PM Pashinyan
articles.summary: Adekvad party leader Artur Danielyan was arrested for criticizing Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Facebook, with charges stemming from his online activity.
articles.content: Armenia has seen a surge in arrests of opposition figures over the past two years, with many charges stemming from their online activity. The latest incident involves Artur Danielyan, leader of the opposition party Adekvad, who was arrested after criticizing Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Facebook. The grounds for Danielyan's detention were his Facebook posts, which targeted both Pashinyan and Armenia's security services. A key point of contention was Pashinyan's stance on a possible prisoner exchange with Azerbaijan, where an Azerbaijani soldier is accused of breaking into the home of a 39-year-old woman in an Armenian village. Pashinyan had ruled out swapping the soldier for detained Armenians in Azerbaijan in an interview with Infocom. Danielyan responded to this decision with a scathing attack on Pashinyan, calling him a "scumbag" and accusing him of being unwilling to bring his fellow citizens home. The conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh has left a lasting impact on the region. After Azerbaijan's military offensive in 2023, Baku regained control over the territory, forcing over 100,000 Armenians to flee their homes. Currently, there are 19 Armenian individuals being held in detention in Baku. Armenia's civil society representatives have expressed concern that this wave of arrests signals a worrying turn toward democratic backsliding. They argue that selective justice undermines trust in the rule of law and may have far-reaching consequences for Armenia's relations with the European Union. Armenian civil society organizations have come out in force against what they see as selective prosecution of critics of the government. The joint statement from over a dozen organizations describes the charges brought against Adekvad party leader as "patently illegal, disproportionate, and politically motivated. Critics argue that these actions are not just punitive but also serve to silence dissenting voices and stifle public debate. Several other activists have faced prosecution for speaking out against the ruling establishment or Prime Minister Pashinyan. The case of Artur Osipyan is a notable example: he was arrested after a verbal clash with Pashinyan over Nagorno-Karabakh policy, and later charged with disrupting public order and obstructing the ruling party's campaign. Osipyan was also accused of inciting violence against Pashinyan in a social media post from March. articles.title: Researchers at University of Oxford Simulate Complex Particle Interactions Using Quantum Computer Setup
articles.summary: A breakthrough in simulating complex particle interactions has been made by researchers using a unique quantum computer setup, allowing for the study of lattice gauge theories in higher dimensions.
articles.content: Researchers at the University of Oxford have made a significant breakthrough in simulating complex particle interactions using a unique quantum computer setup. In a new study published in Nature Physics, they successfully demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a lattice gauge theory. Lattice gauge theories are crucial for understanding how matter interacts with fundamental forces such as electromagnetism and the strong nuclear force. These theories form the foundation of the Standard Model of particle physics, which describes the behavior of subatomic particles. In a lattice gauge theory, space is represented as a grid with particles located at its vertices and gauge fields connecting them. Quantum simulators have emerged as powerful tools for studying these complex interactions. However, most previous simulations of the simplest version of lattice gauge theory, known as Z₂, were limited to one spatial dimension, where certain effects cannot appear. This restriction has hindered scientists' ability to fully explore the behavior of particles in higher dimensions. To overcome this limitation, the Oxford researchers employed a novel approach using trapped ions, which serve two purposes simultaneously. The electronic states of these ions encode gauge fields, while their vibrations represent matter. By harnessing the unique properties of trapped ions, the team was able to simulate a Z₂ lattice gauge theory in a quasi-two-dimensional loop. The experiment's success has opened up new avenues for researchers seeking to understand complex particle interactions. To learn more about this groundbreaking study, Phys.org spoke with Sebastian Saner, the first author of the research paper. Saner revealed that the idea of using entangled qubits to encode gauge-field flux was a pivotal moment in the project's development. This innovative approach allowed the team to simulate lattice gauge theories in higher dimensions and explore effects previously inaccessible to researchers. The team's innovative approach used two trapped ions to create a closed loop, allowing them to study the effects of stored entangled qubit flux on a moving particle. This setup is crucial in understanding how particles interact with each other through gauge fields. Gauge theories describe how particles such as electrons repel or attract each other through various fields. In these theories, matter fields represent the particles themselves, while gauge fields mediate their interactions. For instance, two electrons interacting through the electromagnetic field would be described by a gauge theory. Some of the most fascinating materials in physics, including quantum spin liquids and high-temperature superconductors, are also governed by gauge theories. In these cases, the collective behavior of electrons gives rise to gauge fields that emerge from their interactions. Physicists often use Z₂ lattice gauge theories to study these materials, as they provide a simplified yet still accurate representation. Z₂ lattice gauge theories describe systems where links on a grid can take only two values: present or absent. This is the simplest type of gauge theory and has been used to model topological quantum error correction. Theories in this category are particularly relevant when studying materials with complex electron behavior. Simulating these theories on classical computers poses significant challenges, especially as the system size increases. Computational complexity grows exponentially with system size, making it difficult to study systems in higher dimensions. As a result, researchers often rely on experimental methods to study gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, links can form closed loops that can be pierced by magnetic flux, giving rise to quasiparticles called visons. These particles have no counterpart in one dimension, where loop formation is not possible. Researchers have used various experimental approaches to study Z₂ lattice gauge theories, but most of these methods are limited to one-dimensional setups or simplified models. The researchers have found a way to simulate Aharonov-Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory using trapped ions. These ions are unique because they possess both qubits and vibrational modes, but typically their vibrations are cooled down to facilitate interactions between qubits. However, the team decided to utilize both properties of the ions. The electronic energy levels of a strontium ion were used as qubits to represent the gauge field on a link, while its vibrations behaved like harmonic oscillators to serve as matter sites. This dual approach allowed for a more efficient storage of matter fields in the vibrational modes. In this simulation, a single phonon represents a matter particle, and an oscillator can hold any number of units of vibrational energy or phonons. The advantage of using vibrational modes is that they can store matter fields much more efficiently than usual methods. The geometry of the lattice is determined by which qubits and vibrational modes are coupled together, rather than the physical positions of the ions. This allows for the creation of synthetic dimensions, even with the ions in a single line, where loops and other geometries can be formed. To make the phonon hop between sites, the researchers applied two forces using a laser, each acting on a different vibrational mode and pushing in a direction set by the qubit's state. This process ties the particle's motion to the gauge field, as required by the theory. The hopping of particles between sites causes the field line on the link to switch between present and absent, mimicking the behavior described in lattice gauge theories. To further explore the behavior of particles within a lattice gauge theory, the team introduced a second ion into the system, effectively creating a loop and giving the particle two paths to choose from when traversing between matter sites. The addition of this second qubit allowed for the encoding of flux through the loop by entangling the link qubits. This resulted in two distinct entangled states: one corresponding to zero flux, and the other representing a nonzero flux or vison. According to Saner, the researchers faced significant challenges in translating theoretical concepts into practical experiment design. They needed to achieve precise control over hybrid interactions, develop effective state preparation techniques, and optimize readout methods. The team observed that when a single ion was used to simulate one link between two matter sites, the particle exhibited tunneling behavior, switching between present and absent field lines as it moved back and forth between the sites. This phenomenon aligns with the Z₂ version of Gauss's law. As the particle moved away from its starting site, a field line would emerge behind it but disappear upon return to the initial site. Initially, the researchers set the energy cost for creating a field line to zero, resulting in oscillations that were both fast and large-scale. However, when this cost was introduced, the particle's movement became energetically costly due to the need to constantly create new field lines. The introduction of an energy cost led to significant changes in particle behavior, as moving between sites became increasingly difficult due to the energetic expense of creating a field line with each move. This suppression of tunneling is seen as a precursor to confinement in larger systems, where quarks are bound together within hadrons. The researchers have observed that the trapped ions exhibit behavior consistent with the Aharonov-Bohm effect when they pass through a loop of two entangled qubits in a lattice gauge theory. In this setup, each link in the loop acts as one of the paths around a region with magnetic flux. As the ion crosses a link, it acquires a phase determined by that link's gauge field, which is either positive or negative in the Z₂ case. The experiment demonstrates how the entanglement state of the qubits affects the motion of the ions. When the qubits are in a zero-flux state, both paths contribute positively to the ion's phase, resulting in free tunneling between sites, twice as fast as on a single link. However, when the qubits are entangled in a vison state, representing magnetic flux, the two paths give opposite contributions to the ion's phase. As a result, the particle remains stationary, with its tunneling completely suppressed due to interference. The researchers also verified that the magnetic flux within the loop remains constant over time, except for a gradual decay caused by decoherence from environmental noise sources such as heating of vibrational modes. Numerical simulations incorporating these noise effects matched closely with the experimental data obtained from the trapped ions. According to the team, this study showcases how the hybrid approach can accurately capture the impact of magnetic flux on matter transport in lattice gauge theories. The researchers are looking to expand their approach beyond its current limitations. They plan to apply it to more complex lattice gauge theories by allowing the gauge field to take on multiple values. This would involve extending the Z₂ model to higher dimensions, such as Zₙ, where n represents a larger number of possible gauge field values. The team is also considering pushing the limit of the number of gauge field values towards infinity. The ultimate goal is to develop a more comprehensive understanding of how magnetic flux affects matter transport in lattice gauge theories. articles.title: Ancient Maya's Use of Red Paint Linked to Mercury Poisoning
articles.summary: A new study reveals that the ancient Maya civilization's extensive use of cinnabar in their red paint led to mercury poisoning in lakes and waterways.
articles.content: The use of red paint by the ancient Maya civilization has been linked to environmental disaster. A new study reveals that the Maya's extensive use of cinnabar, a vibrant red pigment made from mercury-sulfide mineral, led to the poisoning of their lakes and waterways with mercury. Cinnabar was a common ingredient in the paint used by the Maya, who were known for their love of the color red. They applied it to almost everything, including sculptures, monuments, walls, plazas, pottery, and even the dead as part of ceremonial funerals. This widespread use of cinnabar led to the contamination of nearby waterways. When the paint ran off into lakes and rivers, anaerobic bacteria in the sediments transformed the cinnabar into highly toxic methylmercury. Over time, this substance accumulated in the food chain, posing a significant threat to the environment. The Maya's use of red paint is an example of how human activities can have unintended consequences on the environment. Their passion for the color red, which represented the sun, blood, and life, ultimately led to environmental disaster. The Maya's reliance on freshwater resources was a crucial aspect of their daily lives, and they heavily depended on fisheries for protein, including freshwater shellfish. Previous research had already indicated high levels of mercury in certain regions of the Maya's territory, but its presence in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula remained unexamined until now. Researchers decided to investigate this area, specifically looking at mud sediments from the region for signs of mercury poisoning. The study focused on two sites: Cobá Lake and Cenote Xcach, a flooded sinkhole beside a ruined city. At these locations, sediment cores were analyzed for mercury levels, revealing extreme concentrations that hinted at widespread use of cinnabar paint, a likely source of the toxic mineral. The amounts of mercury detected in the sediment cores were staggering, with some samples containing as much as 820 parts per billion. For context, authorities consider water with mercury levels above 2 parts per billion to be unsafe for consumption, while any fish exceeding 1 part per million can be seized. These findings suggest that the Maya's use of cinnabar paint was far more extensive than previously thought, and it is likely that this excessive use contributed to environmental disasters in their region. The presence of mercury in the waterways around the ancient Maya civilization's cities has been confirmed through an analysis of sediment cores. Researchers have found that these sediment cores contain high levels of mercury, a toxic substance that can cause severe poisoning when ingested or absorbed through the skin. In humans, mercury poisoning can lead to permanent damage to internal organs and brain function, as well as death. The team discovered mercury levels in excess of 3 parts per million in some areas, which is far higher than the threshold at which poisoning becomes a significant health risk. This excessive exposure to mercury would have had devastating consequences for the people living in these regions. The presence of mercury in the water at Cenote Xcach suggests a long-standing problem that may have contributed to the collapse of the Maya civilization. The sediment cores revealed that mercury levels were high during the Preclassic and Classic periods, but by the time of the collapse, these levels had begun to decrease in many areas. The cinnabar used to create the vibrant red paint must have been imported from outside the Yucatán region, likely from what is now Honduras. This importation continued until the collapse, as evidenced by the mercury poisoning that persisted at Cenote Xcach during this time. articles.content: The moon's volcanic past may have been more active than previously thought, with new research suggesting that Earth's gravity played a key role in keeping its interior hot for billions of years. For decades, scientists have believed that the moon cooled rapidly after its formation around 4.5 billion years ago, when a massive protoplanet collided with early Earth. However, samples returned from China's Chang'e-5 mission revealed surprising evidence of volcanic activity on the moon, dating back to just 2 billion years ago. This finding has left scientists puzzled, as it seems to defy the laws of physics that dictate how planets and moons cool over time. With a relatively small size, the moon should have lost its internal heat quickly after forming, rendering it geologically dormant. A new study published in the journal Planet proposes an explanation for this phenomenon: tidal heating caused by Earth's gravitational pull on the moon. The researchers suggest that this force may have kept the moon's interior hot and active, allowing for volcanic activity to persist long after its formation. The idea of tidal heating is not new, but it has been largely overlooked in previous studies of the moon's evolution. According to the research team, Earth's gravity would have caused the moon's interior to heat up due to friction generated by the tidal forces acting on its crust and mantle. The age of the lunar basalts returned by China's Chang'e-5 mission has raised questions about the moon's volcanic activity in the distant past. Laboratory analysis revealed that these rocks are approximately 2 billion years old, which is puzzling given that traditional geological theory suggests volcanoes should not have existed on the moon at this time. Scientists have proposed various explanations for this anomaly, but none of them seem to fit the available data. Radioactive elements, such as potassium and uranium, could potentially contribute to heat generation through their decay process. However, there is insufficient undecayed material remaining on the moon to account for the required amount of heat. The researchers considered asteroid impacts as another possible source of thermal energy. These events can cause localized high-impact heating, but the period of intense bombardment that shaped the moon's surface had long since ended by the time the basalts were formed. This means that asteroid strikes are unlikely to be responsible for the observed volcanic activity. Tidal forces have been identified as a potential alternative explanation for the heat generated within the early moon. These forces, which occur when a celestial body is stretched and compressed as it orbits its parent body in an elliptical path, may have caused frictional heating within the moon's interior. This phenomenon is well-documented in other systems, such as Jupiter's moon Io, which experiences frequent volcanic eruptions due to tidal activity. The moon's orbit has undergone significant changes over its history, and two billion years ago it was much closer to Earth than it is today. It orbited our planet in just 16 days, compared to the 27 days it takes now, and its path was more oval-shaped than circular. As a result, Earth's gravity exerted strong tidal forces on the moon's interior during each orbit. Astronomers have long understood the impact of these gravitational squeezes, but their models of the moon's interior have been simplified to assume a uniform spherical shape. However, scientists knew that this was not entirely accurate, as there is a layer of rock with low viscosity between the moon's core and mantle. This zone plays a crucial role in how the tidal forces affect the moon. When researchers used a more realistic 3D representation of the mantle setup in their convection simulations, they noticed a significant amount of energy being directed towards two specific regions along the lunar core-mantle boundary. These areas are now known as tidal heating anomaly zones (THAZs), and they have a profound impact on the moon's internal dynamics. The researchers calculated that around 3.2 billion years ago, these THAZs were subjected to an enormous amount of energy due to tidal strain. Despite making up only a small portion of the mantle, just 2.5% of its total volume, they absorbed over 150 gigawatts of power. This is equivalent to more than four times the amount of energy generated by radioactive decay. This immense energy input would have had a profound impact on the moon's volcanic activity, potentially keeping its internal heat sources active and driving geological processes for extended periods. The significance of this phenomenon is not unique to Earth's moon, as other systems, such as Jupiter's moon Io, also experience similar tidal effects that drive frequent volcanic eruptions. The moon's geological history has long been a topic of study and debate among scientists. A new theory suggests that Earth's gravity played a significant role in keeping the lunar core warm for an extended period, which in turn helped sustain a magnetic field. This prolonged warmth allowed the moon to maintain its magnetic field longer than previously thought, a discovery that was initially puzzling given the findings from Apollo missions. The samples collected during these missions indicated that they formed in a strong magnetic field, contradicting earlier predictions. The theory also proposes that Earth's gravity drove massive mantle plumes towards the lunar crust. These plumes eventually cooled and solidified, producing the basalts seen in the Chang'e-5 samples. Despite offering some answers to long-standing questions about the moon's geological history, this new model is still just a theory and requires further validation. The next decade promises to bring numerous lunar missions that could provide more definitive data on the moon's evolution. The success of these missions will depend on their ability to gather accurate and comprehensive information on the moon's composition and internal structure. The study suggests that Earth's gravitational pull may have played a crucial role in maintaining the moon's volcanic activity during its early stages. This theory is based on simulations of tidal heating at the core-mantle boundary of the moon. The researchers propose that Earth's gravity caused tidal heating, which would have kept the moon's volcanic heart active for millions of years. If this scenario holds true, it could provide a new explanation for the moon's geological history and its unique composition. The study's findings offer valuable insights into the complex relationship between our planet and its satellite. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-earth-gravity-early-moon-volcanic.html
